Activity 3.1.2: Development, support and promotion of Online Database With a private partner, the project developed and launched the cutting-edge digital technology for job-match between job-seekers and employers, and for upskilling their capacities. The mobile application “IshtApp” offers the unemployed and employers the opportunity to get real-life, responsive and interactive solutions to meet their needs in searching jobs and adequate workforce respectively. Those registered with the mobile application now have the opportunity to link with potential employers, or vice versa, so the employers can find needful workforce and also get to know the latest trends in the labor market. They use the platform to learn what occupations, qualifications and skills are in demand at the time. The mobile application’s feature collects and processes data on current trends regularly from specialized open sources and offers ready-to-use information to both end users. The online platform reaches out to the unemployed to help them access jobs they are seeking or become capable of marketing themselves out. The mobile application helps bring the supply and demand side of the labour market together, focusing on the most vulnerable target groups, typically those that operate in the shadow economy. More specifically, it helps over 7,000 recently unemployed, mostly daily labourers (women, youth, minorities, etc.) to register online in the application that also helps them link to new employment by deploying an innovative matching system. On 18 May 2021, the project launched the official kick-off and presentation of the “Ishtapp” mobile application. One week after the launch, the following statistics and achievements about the “Ishtapp” job-match application had become available: • 4,451 users registered with the application; • over 200 employers; • 475 vacancies placed; • 2,019 resumes or applications submitted; • 10,600 downloads. Within first 2 weeks, the project achieved one of the key performance indicators (KPI) obtaining 3,000 users. As of October 22, 2021 the mobile application IshtApp reached 17 860 installations/downloads, 7 239 registered users, 410 employers, 1 514 vacancies and 4 892 sent CVs.
Activity 3.1.3: MSME Support Facility. “Business Advisory Support Facility” is a mechanism to support micro-, small, and medium enterprises (MSME) that suffered from the effects of the COVID-19. This approach has proven its effectiveness and agility as a straightforward way of delivering business-consultancy and financial assistance to entrepreneurs who need help to restart their businesses, reinstate cut jobs and create new ones. The Business Advisory Support Facility places a special emphasis on women-leg enterprises and offers the following activities to effectively restart business operations: • Providing financial support to MSMEs through the on-granting modality; • Supplementing the financial support with business advisory services.
The facility supported 32 MSMEs from throughout Kyrgyzstan, where 30 are owned by women. An average ticket size per MSME was USD 5,900. The project engaged two local CSOs as responsible partners to administer the facility. The total budget of this activity was USD 240,000. Both partner-CSOs reported that the 32 MSMEs’ grant projects were expected to support a total of 395 jobs, which includes newly created and reinstated jobs.
Activity 3.1.4: Export Market Re-orientation Research The purpose of the research, or strategy, was to offer a guidance to the Ministry of Economy of the Kyrgyz Republic on intervention in foreign trade and revision of the Export Development Plan of the Government to 2023 (EDP). In the short run, the Strategy proposes to revisit new goals in the context of reorientation of export markets for the current EDP. First of all, the objectives are conditioned by the fact that in the near future, no increase of exported goods is expected, since the government programs in this area have not yet been adopted. Also, dedicated human resources are unlikely to be increased. In this regard, the study proposes to focus on the situation as is and to work with exporters to: (1) diversify export markets, and (2) maintain the current number of exporters.
In addition, the results of the analysis, on a medium-term basis, provide guidance to the Ministry of Agriculture of the Kyrgyz Republic on the types of products to potentially focus on increasing the production volumes, and steps to take to increase exports. It suggests focusing on the diversification of foreign markets and maintaining the position in the existing markets, with the establishment of key performance indicators, addressing barriers to border crossing and settlement of prices for air-cargo services, and maintaining the number of existing exporters. It further touches upon the access to finance, VAT reimbursement, quality infrastructure, barriers at the border with neighboring countries, intensification of the economic diplomacy, creation of conditions in the domestic market, and the like. 45 companies participated in the interviews: among which 3 companies are non-exporters (led by women), and the remaining 42 companies are exporters. Out of the 42 suppliers, 21 are represented by women. In this regard, the conclusions explain reasons why exports are currently not growing and make recommendations as to what is important to support Kyrgyzstan’s exporters today.
